subject: Archaeology
title: Roman Bridges That Still Stand
description: A fast breakdown of Roman Bridges That Still Stand for builders.

hook.text: Cars drive across Roman bridges in Spain every day. The bridges are over 2,000 years old and carry modern traffic.

buildup.text: The Alcántara Bridge in Spain spans the Tagus River with six arches and stands 150 feet above the water.

discovery.text: An inscription on the bridge reads: 'I have built a bridge that will last forever.' The engineer was not wrong.

twist.text: During wars, armies destroyed arches to stop enemies. Each time, the bridge was repaired and kept serving.

climax.text: Roman arch design distributes weight so efficiently that it requires no mortar. Gravity holds the stones in place.

punchline.text: A Roman engineer promised forever. Two thousand years later, he was right.

quiz.question: What makes Roman arch bridges so durable?
options: They used iron reinforcement hidden inside the stones
The arch design distributes weight so efficiently that no mortar is needed
They were built with a special type of waterproof stone

details.summary: Hundreds of Roman bridges survive across Europe and the Middle East, many still carrying traffic after 2,000 years. Their semicircular arches, concrete foundations, and careful stone fitting created structures so durable that some, like Spain's Alcántara Bridge, remain functional today.
details.whyItMatters: Roman bridges demonstrate that well-engineered infrastructure can outlast the civilization that built it by millennia. Their longevity challenges our assumptions about the lifespan of modern construction.
takeaways: Hundreds of Roman bridges survive after 2,000 years
Semicircular arches and concrete foundations ensured durability
Some bridges like Alcántara still carry modern traffic

faq.question: Which Roman bridge is the most impressive?
faq.answer: The Alcántara Bridge in Spain, spanning the Tagus River, stands 48 meters high and was completed in 106 CE. Its inscription reads: 'I have built a bridge that will last forever.' Nearly 2,000 years later, it still carries vehicles, vindicating that bold claim.

faq.question: How did Romans build bridges across rivers?
faq.answer: They used cofferdams — temporary wooden enclosures driven into the riverbed and pumped dry — to build foundation piers in flowing water. Once the piers were set, wooden centering frameworks supported the arches during construction until the keystone was placed and the arch became self-supporting.
